hero.label: Made for Business
hero.headline: I want to help build your first revenue engine from scratch.
hero.subheadline: Early-stage startups live or die by their ability to find and close the right customers before the runway runs out. I have spent the last year doing exactly that as a BDR and a digital marketing intern, and I want to bring that scrappiness to your team this summer. The Business Development Intern role feels like the right seat at the right moment.

whyCompany.title: Early-stage BD is about testing fast and learning faster
whyCompany.body: At this stage, business development is less about polished playbooks and more about figuring out which channels, messages, and targets actually convert. I thrive in that experimental environment because I have had to build outreach sequences from scratch without a template to copy. That zero-to-one energy is where I do my best work.

whyCompany.title: Summer 2026 is a critical growth window for an early team
whyCompany.body: Hiring a BD intern right now signals that the team is ready to accelerate customer conversations and stress-test the go-to-market motion. I want to be the person who helps sharpen that motion before it scales. Joining early means my work will actually shape how the company develops its sales culture, not just execute what already exists.

whyCompany.title: I have cold-called and converted for a startup before
whyCompany.body: At Copygen.ai I ran cold outreach end-to-end using HubSpot and LinkedIn sequences and helped bring in 15 to 20 paying clients as one of the first sales hires. At NextAfter I learned how digital touchpoints and messaging strategy drive B2B pipeline. Those two experiences together give me a practical foundation that most interns my age simply do not have yet.

quote: I did not wait for a big company to teach me sales. I learned it by doing the uncomfortable work at a startup, and now I want to bring that to a team that is still in the building phase.
